title: Bump agnix-core 0.54.0 → 0.56.1 in osf
summary: A dependency-only change: the `osf` crate pins `agnix-core` to `=0.56.1` instead of `=0.54.0`, and Cargo.lock follows with `agnix-core` 0.56.1 and its transitive `agnix-rules` 0.56.5. No source in this repository changes; the blast radius is whatever `osf` does with the agnix rule engine at runtime, so the map below shows the unchanged callers and the swapped crate boundary.

lanes.label: osf crate
lanes.subtitle: Rust workspace member
lanes.summary: The crate whose manifest pin moved. Its source is untouched; only the version it resolves against changed.

lanes.label: agnix engine
lanes.subtitle: crates.io dependency
lanes.summary: The lint/rule engine consumed by osf. Both the core crate and its rules data crate moved forward two minor versions.

lanes.label: Cargo registry
lanes.subtitle: crates.io + lockfile
lanes.summary: Where the new versions are resolved from and recorded. Cargo.lock is the only file besides the manifest that changed.

nodes.label: osf
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf
nodes.summary: The workspace crate that depends on agnix-core. Nothing inside it changed in this diff; it is the consumer whose behavior the version bump can affect.

nodes.label: osf Cargo.toml
nodes.subtitle: agnix-core = "=0.56.1"
nodes.summary: The single edited line: the exact-version pin on agnix-core moves from 0.54.0 to 0.56.1. The `=` prefix keeps the pin exact, so no other version can satisfy it.

nodes.label: agnix-core
nodes.summary: The rule engine crate osf calls into. Two minor versions of upstream change arrive at once, including whatever new API surface or rule behavior 0.55 and 0.56 introduced.

nodes.label: agnix-rules
nodes.summary: The rules data crate pulled in transitively by agnix-core. Its version moved independently of the core crate, which is why the two numbers do not match.

nodes.label: Cargo.lock
nodes.subtitle: resolved versions + checksums
nodes.summary: Records the resolved agnix-core 0.56.1 and agnix-rules 0.56.5 with their new checksums, so every build of this commit gets the same artifacts.

nodes.label: crates.io
nodes.subtitle: registry index
nodes.summary: The upstream source of the new crate versions. Unchanged by this diff, but it is where the new checksums were fetched from.

edges.summary: The pin that this change is about: osf now requires exactly agnix-core 0.56.1 rather than 0.54.0.

edges.label: rule engine
edges.summary: The existing compile-time dependency from osf's source onto the agnix rule engine. Unchanged in shape, but it is the path along which the version bump reaches runtime behavior.
agnix-core's own dependency on the rules data crate, resolved to 0.56.5 in the new lockfile.

edges.label: version + checksum
edges.summary: The lockfile entry that pins the resolved agnix-core artifact and its checksum.

edges.label: version + checksum
edges.summary: The lockfile entry for the transitively resolved rules crate.
The registry serves the new crate version that the lockfile now records.

flows.title: Resolving the new agnix pin
flows.summary: What happens on the next `cargo build`/`cargo update` after the pin moves: the manifest constraint selects agnix-core 0.56.1, which drags agnix-rules 0.56.5 along, and the lockfile records both.

messages.label: resolve agnix-core =0.56.1
messages.note: The exact pin means the resolver has no freedom: 0.56.1 or nothing.

messages.label: agnix-rules 0.56.5
messages.note: Transitive dependency resolved independently of the core crate's own version number.

views.title: osf ↔ agnix dependency boundary
views.summary: The whole change sits on one boundary: the exact-version pin from the osf crate to the agnix rule engine, and the lockfile entries that record the resolved artifacts.

views.title: Inside the agnix engine
views.summary: The two crates that moved together: agnix-core and the agnix-rules data crate it depends on, both resolved to new versions in the lockfile.
